prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: whether the home policy covers flooding. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the member says rain entered through a blocked gutter, downpipe, roof defect or overflowing drain, I treat it as surface water or maintenance-related ingress rather than flood, so I check the exact source before I mention cover."},{"type":"fact","content":"When water comes from a river, stream, the sea or a tidal surge, I treat that as flood for policy purposes and then check whether any flood exclusion, excess or endorsement applies."},{"type":"observation","content":"When there has been heavy rainfall but the water only entered through doors, airbricks, vents or a low threshold, I do not assume flood cover applies unless the entry was from general flooding outside the home."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member mentions groundwater rising through the floor or walls, I treat that as flood only if the policy wording includes groundwater; otherwise I flag it for review because some wordings distinguish it from standard flood."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the garden, driveway or garage is wet but the inside of the home stayed dry, I note the event carefully, because external standing water alone does not always mean an insured flood loss."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a local authority, the Environment Agency or the Met Office reports flooding in the area, I use that as supporting evidence of a flood event, but I still confirm that the damage mechanism matches the policy definition."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the claim arises after a storm, I separate wind-driven rain and storm damage from flood, because members often describe them together even though the policy treatment can differ."},{"type":"fact","content":"When flood water entered alongside sewage or contaminated water from an overwhelmed drain or sewer, I check whether the policy covers resulting damage, because the drainage cause and the contamination can affect the assessment."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the evidence is unclear, I prefer to ask for photos, the timeline of the event and any repair notes before I decide on flood cover, because a quick label can be wrong."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the claim is for a flat, maisonette or basement, I pay extra attention to the elevation and the route of ingress, because flood cover can turn on whether the water came from outside at ground level or from another source."}]}
